deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.2 端緒 — Grammar & Expressions
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第二章「端緒」
notes: Grammar and expressions for Chapter 2: casual and rough male speech (すげえ, 〜ぞ／〜ぜ, 〜かよ, 〜ちゃう), first-person pronoun play, and the language of bewilderment and realisation (〜にしては, 身に覚えがない, まさか). Built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style, not transcribed page by page, so a few items may turn up a chapter early or late. Example sentences are original, not quoted from the book.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.scene: 瀧 keeps thinking that, for a dream, everything feels far too real.
cards.context: Form: N / V plain form + にしては. The result doesn't match what you'd expect from that premise: 夢にしてはリアル, 初めてにしては上手. Compare 〜わりに (similar, but can follow adjectives: 高いわりに) and 〜としては (from the standpoint of).
cards.example_sentence: 初めて作ったにしては、このケーキはよくできている。
cards.example_reading: はじめて つくった に しては、 この ケーキ は よく できて いる。
cards.example_meaning: For a first attempt, this cake turned out really well.
cards.pattern: N / V plain form + にしては

cards.scene: The strange room, the strange body — 瀧 concludes it can only be a dream.
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adj may drop だ) + としか思えない. Lit. 'can't think anything other than ~' — strong conviction, often about something odd. Same frame: 〜としか言えない 'all I can say is ~'.
cards.example_sentence: こんなに偶然が重なるなんて、運命としか思えない。
cards.example_reading: こんな に ぐうぜん が かさなる なんて、 うんめい と しか おもえない。
cards.example_meaning: With so many coincidences piling up, it can only be fate.
cards.pattern: plain form + としか思えない

meanings: to feel bewitched (as if tricked by a fox)
cards.scene: The morning after a swap, each hero feels as if they had been tricked by a fox.
cards.context: Form: 狐につままれる, usually 狐につままれたような顔 / 気分. In folklore foxes 'pinch' (つまむ) people and bewitch them, so the idiom means being baffled by something that makes no sense. Fits a story steeped in the supernatural.
cards.example_sentence: 起きたら部屋がきれいに片付いていて、狐につままれたような気分だった。
cards.example_reading: おきたら へや が きれい に かたづいて いて、 きつね に つままれた よう な きぶん だった。
cards.example_meaning: I woke up to find my room neatly tidied, and felt completely bewildered.
cards.pattern: 狐につままれた(ような) + 顔／気分

cards.scene: 瀧 at 三葉's school — which desk was hers again? Which classroom?
cards.context: Form: plain form (often past: だった／したっけ) + っけ; polite 〜でしたっけ／〜ましたっけ. Asks yourself or someone to confirm something you half-remember. Very common in speech, never in formal writing.
cards.example_sentence: あれ、今日の集合時間は何時だったっけ？
cards.example_reading: あれ、 きょう の しゅうごう じかん は なんじ だった っけ？
cards.example_meaning: Huh, what time were we meeting today again?

cards.scene: 四葉 has to call her big sister more than once, and she's running out of patience.
cards.context: Form: sentence + ってば (insisting: もういいってば！ 'I said it's fine!') or name + ってば (exasperation: お姉ちゃんってば…). Contracted from といえば. Softer variant: 〜ったら (お姉ちゃんったら).
cards.example_sentence: だから、私じゃないってば！
cards.example_reading: だから、 わたし じゃ ない って ば！
cards.example_meaning: I told you, it wasn't me!

cards.scene: Both heroes do things in each other's bodies that can't be undone — and talk about them in casual speech.
cards.context: Form: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう, 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう (past 〜ちゃった／〜じゃった). Completion or regret: 寝坊しちゃった, 全部飲んじゃった. A rougher male version is 〜ちまう／〜ちまった. Same meaning as 〜てしまう, but casual speech only.
cards.example_sentence: 楽しみにしていたプリン、弟に食べられちゃった。
cards.example_reading: たのしみ に して いた プリン、 おとうと に たべられちゃった。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother ate the pudding I'd been looking forward to.
cards.pattern: Vて → 〜ちゃう ／ Vで → 〜じゃう

cards.word: すげえ・やべえ (〜い → 〜えー)
meanings: rough male sound change in い-adjectives
cards.scene: Rough boy-speech that sounds natural from 瀧 and his friends — and very strange coming out of 三葉's mouth.
cards.context: Form: the last two vowel sounds of an い-adjective merge into a long え: すごい → すげえ, やばい → やべえ, うるさい → うるせえ, 痛い → いてえ, ない → ねえ (知らねえ). Rough, masculine, very casual. Also written with ー: すげー.
cards.example_reading: うわ、 この けしき すげえ！
cards.pattern: 〜ない → 〜ねえ, 〜ごい → 〜げえ, 〜ばい → 〜べえ, 〜さい → 〜せえ

meanings: neutral / feminine vs. boyish vs. rough masculine 'I'
cards.scene: 三葉, in 瀧's body, tries several words for 'I' before landing on 俺 — while 瀧 says 俺 with 三葉's voice.
cards.context: Form: chosen by speaker, setting and self-image. わたし = neutral; standard for women, and for men in formal settings. わたくし = very formal. あたし = casual feminine. 僕 = soft, polite boyish. 俺 = rough, masculine, among friends. A boy saying わたし casually to his friends sounds odd, so the wrong pronoun instantly marks someone as 'not themselves'.
cards.example_sentence: 仕事では「わたし」と言うが、友達とは「俺」で話している。
cards.example_reading: しごと で は 「わたし」 と いう が、 ともだち と は 「おれ」 で はなして いる。
cards.example_meaning: At work I use the neutral word for 'I', but with friends I use the rough, masculine one.
cards.pattern: わたし／わたくし／あたし／僕／俺

cards.scene: Rough male endings like these are part of what makes 'Mitsuha' sound so unlike herself at school.
cards.context: Form: plain form + ぞ／ぜ (after nouns and な-adj: だぞ, だぜ). ぞ = forceful assertion or warning (行くぞ！ 'Let's go!', 危ないぞ 'Watch out'). ぜ = cool, matey emphasis (行こうぜ). Both sound masculine; a softer, neutral choice is よ.
cards.example_sentence: もう遅いぞ。早く帰ろうぜ。
cards.example_reading: もう おそい ぞ。 はやく かえろう ぜ。
cards.example_meaning: It's late, you know. Let's head home already.

cards.scene: The breezy speech of 瀧's Tokyo friends, which 三葉 has to keep up with.
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adj without だ) + じゃん. From じゃないか; originally Kanto-area slang. Points out the obvious or seeks agreement: いいじゃん！ 'That's great!', 言ったじゃん 'I told you!'. Used by both genders, but very casual.
cards.example_sentence: その服、すごく似合ってるじゃん。
cards.example_reading: その ふく、 すごく にあってる じゃん。
cards.pattern: plain form (N / な-adj without だ) + じゃん

cards.scene: Rough reactions of disbelief — the voice of a boy waking up in a world that makes no sense.
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adj without だ) + かよ. Rhetorical か + emphatic よ: surprise, disbelief or irritation. マジかよ 'No way!', また〜かよ 'Not ~ again!'. Masculine and rough; the neutral version is just a rising tone (本当？).
cards.example_sentence: また雨かよ。せっかくの休みなのに。
cards.example_reading: また あめ かよ。 せっかく の やすみ な のに。
cards.example_meaning: Rain again? And on my day off, too.

cards.scene: 'Taki' suddenly seems oddly girlish to his friends, and 'Mitsuha' boyish to hers.
cards.context: Form: N + っぽい (男っぽい 'boyish', 子供っぽい 'childish'); Vます-stem + っぽい (忘れっぽい 'forgetful'); plain sentence + っぽい (casual 'seems like': 雨が降るっぽい). Vague and casual — compare 〜らしい, which means 'typical of, as it should be' (男らしい 'manly', usually praise).
cards.example_sentence: 今日の彼、なんだか女の子っぽいね。
cards.example_reading: きょう の かれ、 なんだか おんなのこ っぽい ね。
cards.example_meaning: He seems kind of girlish today, doesn't he?
cards.pattern: N / Vます-stem / plain form + っぽい

cards.scene: As 'Taki' works the needle, the tear in 奥寺先輩's skirt becomes something pretty before everyone's eyes.
cards.context: Form: 見る見る(うちに) + a verb of change (〜なる, 〜ていく). Describes a fast change you can actually watch happen: 見る見るうちに暗くなった. Often written みるみる. Compare あっという間に (in an instant, not necessarily watched).
cards.example_sentence: 薬を飲んだら、熱が見る見るうちに下がった。
cards.example_reading: くすり を のんだら、 ねつ が みるみる うち に さがった。
cards.example_meaning: After I took the medicine, my fever went down rapidly.
cards.pattern: 見る見る(うちに) + change verb

cards.scene: Back in their own bodies, each grumbles about what the other did with their day.
cards.context: Form: plain form (N / な-adj + な) + のに at the end of a sentence. The main clause is swallowed, leaving regret, complaint or disappointment: 言ってくれればよかったのに 'You should have told me', せっかく作ったのに 'And after I made it specially…'. Different from mid-sentence のに 'even though'.
cards.example_sentence: 早く起きれば間に合ったのに。
cards.example_reading: はやく おきれば まにあった のに。
cards.example_meaning: If only I'd got up earlier, I would have made it.
cards.pattern: plain form + のに。(at sentence end)

meanings: to have no recollection of doing it
cards.scene: Friends describe things 'they' did yesterday that neither hero remembers doing.
cards.context: Form: 身に覚えがない, or before a noun 身に覚えのない + N. Lit. 'no memory in one's own body' — something is pinned on you that you didn't do (or can't remember doing). Common in denials: 身に覚えのない罪 'a crime I didn't commit'.
cards.example_sentence: 身に覚えのない請求書が届いて、驚いた。
cards.example_reading: み に おぼえ の ない せいきゅうしょ が とどいて、 おどろいた。
cards.example_meaning: I was shocked when a bill arrived for something I never bought.
cards.pattern: 身に覚えがない ／ 身に覚えのない + N

cards.scene: Swapping bodies with a stranger in your sleep? That can't possibly be real — can it?
cards.context: Form: plain form (N + の／である, な-adj + な) + わけがない (casual: わけない). A flat denial based on reasoning. 〜はずがない is close but leans on expectation; 〜わけではない means 'it's not that ~' — don't mix them up.
cards.example_sentence: こんなに難しい問題、一日で解けるわけがない。
cards.example_reading: こんな に むずかしい もんだい、 いちにち で とける わけ が ない。
cards.example_meaning: There's no way I can solve a problem this hard in one day.

cards.scene: Friends' strange reports, odd notes, lost days — slowly the pieces begin to add up.
cards.context: Form: 辻褄が合う／合わない, 辻褄を合わせる (to make a story fit). 辻 (crossroads) + 褄 (the hem of a kimono): seams that line up. Usually about stories or explanations. Often written in kana: つじつま.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の説明は、どうも辻褄が合わない。
cards.example_reading: かれ の せつめい は、 どうも つじつま が あわない。
cards.example_meaning: His explanation just doesn't add up.
cards.pattern: 辻褄が合う ／ 合わない ／ 辻褄を合わせる

cards.scene: The chapter's turning point — could it be that they really are swapping?
cards.context: Form: まさか + negative guess (まさか来ないだろう 'surely he won't come'), まさか〜とは思わなかった 'I never dreamed ~', or alone as an exclamation 'No way!'. Trailing off — まさか… — signals someone realising something unbelievable.
cards.example_sentence: まさか、あれが本当に夢じゃなかったなんて。
cards.example_reading: まさか、 あれ が ほんとう に ゆめ じゃ なかった なんて。
cards.example_meaning: No way — that really wasn't a dream?
cards.pattern: まさか + 〜ない／〜とは思わなかった／…

cards.scene: At first each tries to brush off the strange signs as nothing more than imagination.
cards.context: Form: 気のせいだ 'it's just my imagination'; 気のせいか、〜 'maybe it's just me, but ~'. A way to dismiss a strange feeling — exactly what you tell yourself before admitting something impossible.
cards.example_sentence: 気のせいか、今日はみんなが私を見ている気がする。
cards.example_reading: き の せい か、 きょう は みんな が わたし を みて いる き が する。
cards.example_meaning: Maybe it's just me, but I feel like everyone's looking at me today.
cards.pattern: 気のせいだ ／ 気のせいか、〜
